title: Vector Algebra

notes.heading: 1. Unit Vectors, Direction Cosines & Scalar (Dot) Product
notes.proseLatex: For $\vec{r} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$, magnitude is $|\vec{r}| = \sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}$, unit vector is $\hat{r} = \vec{r}/|\vec{r}|$, and direction cosines $(l,m,n) = (\cos\alpha,\cos\beta,\cos\gamma)$ satisfy $l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$. The scalar product $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\theta = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + a_3 b_3$ tests orthogonality ($\vec{a}\perp\vec{b} \iff \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 0$) and gives scalar projection of $\vec{a}$ along $\vec{b}$ as $\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|}$.

keyFormulas.label: Direction Cosines & Vector Projection
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Direction cosine identities and orthogonal vector projection.

examples.problemLatex: Find the scalar projection of $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ onto $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

notes.heading: 2. Cross Product, Area Formulas & Lagrange's Identity
notes.proseLatex: The vector product $\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\sin\theta\,\hat{n}$ is anti-commutative ($\vec{b}\times\vec{a} = -\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$) and vanishes for nonzero collinear vectors. Geometrically, $|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|$ equals the area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides $\vec{a},\vec{b}$ (and $\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|$ is the triangle area). Lagrange's identity $|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^2 + (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})^2 = |\vec{a}|^2|\vec{b}|^2$ links dot and cross magnitudes without finding $\theta$.

keyFormulas.label: Lagrange's Identity & Parallelogram Area
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute |a x b| directly from |a|, |b|, and a.b.

notes.heading: 3. Scalar & Vector Triple Products (Coplanarity & BAC-CAB)
notes.proseLatex: The scalar triple product $[\vec{a}\;\vec{b}\;\vec{c}] = \vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})$ equals the $3\times 3$ component determinant and represents the signed volume of the parallelepiped; $[\vec{a}\;\vec{b}\;\vec{c}] = 0$ is the exact condition for coplanarity. Cyclic shifts preserve $[\vec{a}\;\vec{b}\;\vec{c}] = [\vec{b}\;\vec{c}\;\vec{a}] = [\vec{c}\;\vec{a}\;\vec{b}]$. The vector triple product expands by the BAC-CAB rule $\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c}$, which lies in the plane of $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$.

keyFormulas.label: Coplanarity Determinant & BAC-CAB Rule
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Expand vector triple products and check four-point coplanarity.

wbjeebTraps: Vector triple product is NOT associative: $\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) \neq (\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}$ in general.
Projection of $\vec{a}$ ON $\vec{b}$ divides by $|\vec{b}|$, NOT $|\vec{a}|$: $\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|}$.
